title: Bangladesh Dual Citizenship and NVR Explained for NRBs: Eligibility, Process and Rights
metaTitle: Bangladesh Dual Citizenship & NVR for NRBs
metaDescription: How dual citizenship and the NVR (No Visa Required) endorsement work for Bangladeshis abroad: who is eligible, documents, process, and what rights you keep.
heroIntro: Millions of Bangladeshis have taken the nationality of the UK, USA, Canada, Australia or other countries. Many wrongly believe they have lost their Bangladeshi identity, or they travel on a foreign passport without the endorsement that lets them enter freely. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Dual Citizenship & NVR
points: The Citizenship Act 1951 and government policy allow Bangladeshi citizens to hold a second nationality in certain countries.
The NVR (No Visa Required) endorsement is stamped on your foreign passport by a Bangladesh Mission or the immigration authority.
With NVR you can enter and leave Bangladesh without a visa and keep rights such as property ownership, subject to the law.
Eligibility, fees and documents change; always check the current rules with the Bangladesh Mission.
If you formally renounced Bangladeshi citizenship, you are normally treated as a foreigner.

toc: What Is Dual Citizenship in Bangladesh?

sections.h2: What Is Dual Citizenship in Bangladesh?
sections.content:
Bangladesh allows its citizens to acquire the citizenship of specified countries without losing Bangladeshi nationality, provided the formalities are followed. People who were born Bangladeshi and later acquired another nationality can continue to be treated as Bangladeshi citizens for many purposes, including holding property, if their status is properly documented.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

NVR stands for "No Visa Required". It is a stamp or sticker in your foreign passport, issued on the basis of your Bangladeshi origin, that works as a visa-free entry permit. It also proves to Bangladeshi authorities that you retain your link to Bangladesh. Many land offices, banks and the Immigration authority ask for it.

• People born as Bangladeshi citizens who have acquired the nationality of an eligible country.
  • Children of Bangladeshi citizens, subject to the Citizenship Act and policy at the time.
  • Spouses of Bangladeshis may get separate long-term visa categories, which are different from NVR.

Always check the current list of eligible countries and conditions, because policy can change by Cabinet or circular.

• Valid foreign passport and a copy of your old Bangladeshi passport, if available.
  • Bangladeshi birth certificate or NID.
  • Evidence of Bangladeshi origin: parents' documents, old passport or certificate.
  • Proof of address and recent photographs.
  • Application form and fee as set by the Mission.

1. Visit the website of the Bangladesh Embassy or High Commission in your country and download the form.
  2. Prepare the documents and book an appointment where required.
  3. Submit the application, fee and passport.
  4. The Mission verifies the documents, and may refer to Dhaka for approval.
  5. Collect your passport with the NVR endorsement. If you are in Bangladesh, the Department of Immigration and Passports handles some cases.

• You can generally own and inherit property as a Bangladeshi citizen, subject to the law. See our property rules guide.
  • You can invest in Bangladesh and open NRB accounts.
  • You may be subject to restrictions on voting, public office or certain government jobs, depending on the law.
  • Consular protection depends on circumstances; the other country may also have a claim to protect you.
  • Some countries restrict dual nationality, so check the rules of your second country too.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

faqs.question: Does Bangladesh allow dual citizenship?
faqs.answer: Yes, for citizens who acquire the nationality of specified countries, under the Citizenship Act and government policy. Check the current list.

faqs.question: What is NVR in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: A No Visa Required endorsement in a foreign passport that allows visa-free entry for Bangladeshi-origin persons.

faqs.question: Do I need NVR to buy land in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: It is not always legally required, but many offices and banks ask for it as proof of your citizenship status.

faqs.question: Can children of NRBs get NVR?
faqs.answer: Often yes, based on parentage and policy, but check the current Mission requirements.

faqs.question: What if I renounced Bangladeshi citizenship?
faqs.answer: You are generally treated as a foreigner and need other visa or investor routes.
